subject: Post-call: FastCart throughput & streaming profile — sizing asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Park <lauren@fastcart.com>
Cc: ops@fastcart.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: FastCart throughput & streaming profile — sizing asks

Hi Lauren — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few concrete asks so our infra and sizing team can give a confident pilot estimate.

TL;DR from discovery: FastCart expects interactive search/autocomplete + expanded product summary responses. Key constraints you highlighted: strict perceived latency (search must feel instant), bursty traffic during campaigns, and streaming-first UX for longer summaries.

What we heard (please correct if I’ve mischaracterized):
- Latency target: p50 perceived < 200ms; p95 perceived target around 700ms (search & short responses).
- Typical response sizes: short searches ~40–120 tokens, expanded summaries ~300–700 tokens.
- Steady baseline traffic: ~5–10 QPS across week; peak windows during promos up to ~80–110 QPS (~10–15x spikes).
- Streaming: client expects first token within ~250–400ms and incremental chunks every ~200–400ms for long outputs.
- Concurrency: estimated concurrent sessions ~120–220 during peak events.

Concrete asks from our side to size throughput & recommend an SLO baseline:
1) Provide a 24‑hour traffic sample (CSV is fine) with timestamped requests, average tokens/request, and a marker for ‘promo’ windows. Example column headers: timestamp, endpoint, tokens_out, tokens_in, user_region. (We’ve attached a blank template: fastcart_token_profile.csv)
2) Confirm the expected peak-to-steady multiplier you want us to assume for pilot sizing (you mentioned ~10x on the call).
3) Any client-side timeouts we should plan for (e.g., close streams after 10s?) and typical session lengths for streaming flows.
4) Are there internal SLAs (e.g., payment/operations) that require p99 latency reporting or retention windows beyond our defaults?

Next steps we’ll take once we have that sample:
- Run a token-based throughput projection and provide a recommended slot allocation and concurrency target.
- Produce an SLO proposal (p50/p95/p99 targets + streaming-first tail goals) — I’ve attached an early draft (slo_proposal.pdf) that we’ll refine.
- If numbers look like what we expect, propose a 2‑week pilot with traffic ramping to 50% of peak for the first week.

If you can drop the CSV and any logs (redact PII) to the Drive link or reply here, we’ll prioritize a sizing estimate by EOD Monday.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: fastcart_token_profile.csv (csv) — template]
[Attachment: slo_proposal.pdf (pdf) — draft SLOs and pilot approach]

From: Lauren Park <lauren@fastcart.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FastCart throughput & streaming profile — sizing asks

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Couple quick clarifications:
- Peak behavior is event-driven; the 10x number is a conservative average across our last three promos — some spikes did exceed that briefly but we can cap expectations at 12x for pilot planning.
- Client-side timeout is currently 12s; we can consider reducing to 10s for the pilot if it helps with resource control.
- We’ll pull a 24‑hour export and remove PII; ops@fastcart.com will drop it into the Drive link by EOD tomorrow.

Also, can you confirm whether your streaming SLOs assume smaller chunk sizes (e.g., 64–128 token frames) or larger batched frames? We’re flexible but want to avoid perceived stutter.

— Lauren
Lauren Park | Head of Product, FastCart

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Park <lauren@fastcart.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FastCart throughput & streaming profile — sizing asks

Thanks Lauren — that helps. Looping in Jonas (runtime) and Neha (capacity) so they can annotate the ask and propose a sensible default. A couple follow-ups from our side:
- For chunk size: our recommended default for streaming-first UX is 128 tokens per chunk for 300–700 token outputs; for short search/autocomplete we typically emit 32–64 token frames. This balances early first-byte latency and downstream reassembly. If FastCart wants smoother incremental updates we can shift to 64 token frames at the cost of increased per-token overhead.
- For the CSV: please include a promo flag so we can easily compute peak windows; if ops wants, we can accept a redacted sample (no user ids).
- Ops question: do you expect multi-region routing (US + EU) immediately or just US for pilot?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- FastCart: drop 24‑hour sample to Drive (ops will do this).
- Redwood: run token-based throughput projection and return a sizing summary + suggested concurrency slot plan.
- Schedule a 45‑minute technical review next Tue with Jonas + Neha + FastCart ops to walk the numbers.

Jonas & Neha, feel free to add sizing assumptions below.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: FastCart throughput & streaming profile — sizing asks

Adding a quick technical read for the sizing doc — high level numbers only (we'll refine with actual CSV):

Assumptions from discovery:
- Steady-state QPS: 6 QPS (avg across core hours)
- Expected peak QPS (promo crest): 90 QPS (15x) — you said 10–12x, we’ll use 12x conservative unless you specify otherwise.
- Average tokens per request: 420 tokens for expanded flows, 80 tokens for search. Weighted average during steady ~210 tokens/request; during peak weighted shifts to 320 tokens/request.
- Steady tokens/sec: 6 QPS * 210 tokens = ~1,260 tokens/sec.
- Peak tokens/sec: 90 QPS * 320 tokens = 28,800 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency estimate: with streaming and incremental output, assume average per-request service time ~1.8s steady, ~2.5s under load; concurrency ~= QPS * latency -> steady concurrency ~11, peak concurrency ~225 (matches your 120–220 range).

Sizing guidance (first-cut):
- Pilot target: provision for 50% of peak tokens/sec as safe initial capacity => ~14k tokens/sec. This gives room for autoscaling and cache hit improvements.
- Instance guidance: on our default quantized runtime, a single slot (A100-equivalent) at low-latency streaming config can handle ~3.5k tokens/sec at target p95 under mixed payloads. That implies ~4–5 slots for pilot baseline, scale to ~9–10 at ~100% peak.
- Streaming SLOs: aim to meet first-byte < 350ms p50 and < 700ms p95 for the pilot. If FastCart moves to 64-token frames we’ll see ~8–12% higher CPU/token overhead.

Requests for FastCart ops:
1) 24‑hour CSV with promo_flag and tokens_out tokens_in split.
2) If available, a 30‑minute high-fidelity sample during a previous promo to calibrate crest behavior.
3) Any existing client timeout telemetry (to validate our assumed 12s).

I’ll draft this into the sizing sheet once we have the CSV and mark up the slo_proposal.pdf with concrete slot counts.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber | Runtime Performance, Redwood Inference
